title: Unify push/pull streaming APIs across Python/TS/Go and introduce retry-shim
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Stabilizes SDK streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go
- Adds a small retry-shim abstraction for portable reauth/retry logic
- Minor public API additions (context manager, stream.close) and version bumps: python 1.7.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v1.3.8
description:
Motivation: multiple downstream teams reported divergent streaming semantics across SDKs (push vs pull, ownership of connection lifecycle, and subtle reauth edge cases when token rotation happens mid-stream). This PR harmonizes the observable API shape and introduces a small builtin retry-shim that standardizes reauth+backoff behavior for streaming consumers across Python, TypeScript, and Go.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Consolidated streaming surface by defining a 'PushPullStream' conceptual model: consumers can opt-in to a push-style callback model or a pull-style iterator/async-iterator; underlying transport is shared. Added a lightweight retry-shim in each SDK that intercepts transient transport errors (401/429/5xx) and performs coordinated token refresh + exponential backoff with jitter. Python: added RedwoodStream context manager (supports with/async with) and Stream.close() for deterministic shutdown; introduced an iterator->async iterator adapter for parity. TypeScript: normalized stream consumer to return an AsyncIterable by default and provided a small pushCallback overload for compatibility; improved TypeScript generics to preserve typed events. Go: introduced PullStream interface (Next(ctx) (Event, error)) alongside an adapter to channel-based push consumers; added connection pool safety checks.

Commits summary: - 7 commits, high-level messages: unify: define push/pull stream interface across SDKs; python: add context manager and retry-shim; ts: default async iterable + push overload; go: PullStream adapter + pool fixes; ci: add cross-sdk e2e for streaming reauth; docs: add quickstart and migration notes.

Files changed (high level): src/python/redwood/stream.py, tests/python/test_stream_retry.py, src/ts/stream/index.ts, src/ts/types/stream.d.ts, src/go/stream/pullstream.go, src/go/stream/adapter.go, docs/sdks/streaming.md, examples/streaming-retry/*.md, ci/workflows/stream-e2e.yml, package.json (ts version bump), setup.cfg (python version bump), go.mod (version bump).

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - The retry-shim is intentionally conservative: max 3 retries, base backoff 150ms, jittered, max backoff 2s. For dedicated deployments where clients manage tokens, the shim is opt-out via a client config flag. - We avoided surface breaking changes by adding small overloads and adapter helpers rather than swapping existing return types; where return types changed (TS defaulting to AsyncIterable) we provided a compatibility overload. - To minimize bundle size in the TS SDK, the shim code is tree-shakeable and split behind a small helper exported only from the streaming entrypoint.

Testing: added unit tests for reauth scenarios in all three SDKs and a cross-language e2e that runs a short-lived local test server to simulate 401 mid-stream and verifies that the shim refreshes tokens and resumes without dropping user events. CI run failed initially on flaky TS test related to backpressure simulation; I reworked the test (deterministic tick-based driver) and reran full matrix.

Merge: squash merge to main after approvals and green CI. Migration guidance is included in docs/sdks/streaming.md and examples/streaming-retry/ migration notes.

changelog_entry: Unify streaming APIs across SDKs and add robust reauth/retry shim to handle token rotation mid-stream. Minor ergonomics improvements (context manager and explicit close) and version bumps.
